scope: Recheck the normative DXF ACIS-carrier contract and compare current public open-source DWG/DXF implementation claims against their documented version, direction, and semantic limits; refine existing implementation/evidence owners without promoting support.

method.kind: Primary Autodesk DXF reference plus current upstream project documentation/source inventory
method.evidenceBoundary: Autodesk documents the listed DXF fields and ordering guidance. ezdxf and LibreDWG pages establish their own published scope and caveats only; mutable documentation, aggregate coverage statements, and class inventories are not pinned runtime observations, independent semantic validation, or proof of libdxfrw behavior. ODA v5.4.1 remains the authority for DWG byte layouts.

evidence.topic: Shared DXF ACIS carrier fields and entity-specific history association
observed: 3DSOLID, REGION, and BODY each document AcDbModelerGeometry, group 70 modeler-format version currently 1, group 1 proprietary data, and optional group 3 continuation chunks.
3DSOLID additionally documents AcDb3dSolid and group 350 as a soft-owner handle to a history object.
The entity tables do not specify embedded SAT/SAB save-version semantics or B-rep validity.
evidence.planUse: Keep carrier framing shared only for documented common fields; retain entity-specific subclass and history-handle handling. Preserve repeated chunk order and keep exact carrier retention, history closure, and semantic solid validity independent. Never infer inner ACIS version from group 70.

evidence.topic: DXF field order versus repeated opaque payload order
observed: Autodesk says entity group order can vary and the reader should not rely on the displayed table order.
This general ordering guidance does not alter the payload meaning of repeated group 1/group 3 chunks or authorize moving data across subclass boundaries.
evidence.planUse: Retain existing generated order-variation controls for independent fields while asserting the original concatenated order of repeated ACIS chunks, subclass boundaries, and history association. No new owner is required.

evidence.topic: ezdxf route scope and geometry ceiling
observed: ezdxf describes itself as a DXF interface, not a DWG/DXF version converter or CAD kernel.
Its ACIS module documents SAT for DXF R2000-R2010 and SAB for R2013/R2018.
Its mesh projection covers flat polygonal faces and explicitly loses curved ACIS faces; general curved geometry requires a kernel.
evidence.planUse: Use only as a pinned DXF structural/flat-polyhedron peer. Keep DWG parsing, arbitrary ACIS/B-rep semantics, and curved-surface qualification outside its evidence grade.

evidence.topic: LibreDWG published coverage and per-version/direction caveats
observed: The current README advertises broad DWG read coverage while noting that some advanced R2010+ objects fail and are skipped.
Its documentation records writer limitations by DWG release and separates stable, unstable, unhandled, and test-coverage-gap inventories.
The linked master documentation is mutable and is not an exact peer runtime pin.
evidence.planUse: At optional comparison time, pin a release/commit and report version, entity, direction, owner path, and emitted/typed/opaque/skipped/rejected disposition per case. Treat headline percentages as non-comparable and do not use peer implementation details as DWG layout authority.

refinesExistingOwners: S2.2/S2.3 DXF ACIS carrier and ACDS routes
nextActions: Continue existing implementation slices using their focused local targets; do not repeat peer runs per slice.
For DXF modeler-carrier changes, vary independent field order but preserve and assert repeated payload chunk order and subclass boundaries.

At a composed peer checkpoint only, pin the peer artifact and report direction, entity, version, owner/block path, and disposition independently for parser, writer, carrier, geometry, and consumer outcomes.

planDelta.validation: Receipt JSON and git diff whitespace validation only; no code or runtime tests were required for this research-only plan refinement.
